passages.text: Now there was another famine in the land, subsequent to the one that had occurred in Abraham’s time. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines at Gerar.
passages.sermon:
A famine happened in the land.
This famine was not the first one.
The first famine happened during Abraham’s time.
Isaac lived in this time of famine.
Isaac went to Abimelech.
Abimelech was king of the Philistines.
Abimelech lived in Gerar.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י רָעָב֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ מִלְּבַד֙ הָרָעָ֣ב הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה בִּימֵ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ יִצְחָ֛ק אֶל־ אֲבִימֶּ֥לֶךְ מֶֽלֶךְ־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים גְּרָֽרָה׃

passages.text: The LORD appeared to Isaac and said, “Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in the land where I tell you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD appeared to Isaac.
The LORD spoke to Isaac.
The LORD said, “Do not go down to Egypt.
Stay in the land that I tell you.
passages.original: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אַל־ תֵּרֵ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יְמָה שְׁכֹ֣ן בָּאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֹמַ֥ר אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Stay in this land as a foreigner, and I will be with you and bless you. For I will give all these lands to you and your offspring, and I will confirm the oath that I swore to your father Abraham.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Isaac.
God told Isaac to stay in this land as a foreigner.
God said, "I will be with you."
God said, "I will bless you."
God said, "I will give all these lands to you."
God said, "I will give these lands to your offspring."
God said, "I will keep the oath I swore to your father Abraham."
passages.original: גּ֚וּר בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְאֶֽהְיֶ֥ה עִמְּךָ֖ וַאֲבָרְכֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי־ לְךָ֣ וּֽלְזַרְעֲךָ֗ אֶתֵּן֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָֽאֲרָצֹ֣ת הָאֵ֔ל וַהֲקִֽמֹתִי֙ אֶת־ הַשְּׁבֻעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתִּי לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם אָבִֽיךָ׃

passages.text: I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give them all these lands, and through your offspring all nations of the earth will be blessed, because Abraham listened to My voice and kept My charge, My commandments, My statutes, and My laws.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Isaac.
The LORD promised to bless Isaac.
The LORD said, “I will make your descendants very many.
Your descendants will be as numerous as the stars in the sky.
I will give all these lands to your descendants.
All nations on earth will be blessed through your offspring.
I will do this because Abraham obeyed Me.
Abraham listened to My voice.
Abraham kept My charge.
Abraham kept My commandments.
Abraham kept My statutes.
Abraham kept My laws.”
passages.original: וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֤י אֶֽת־ זַרְעֲךָ֙ כְּכוֹכְבֵ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְנָתַתִּ֣י לְזַרְעֲךָ֔ אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הָאֲרָצֹ֖ת הָאֵ֑ל וְהִתְבָּרֲכ֣וּ בְזַרְעֲךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃ עֵ֕קֶב אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁמַ֥ע אַבְרָהָ֖ם בְּקֹלִ֑י וַיִּשְׁמֹר֙ מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֔י מִצְוֺתַ֖י חֻקּוֹתַ֥י וְתוֹרֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: So Isaac settled in Gerar.
passages.sermon: Isaac was Abraham’s son.\r\nIsaac obeyed God’s command.\r\nIsaac lived in the land of Gerar.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב יִצְחָ֖ק בִּגְרָֽר׃

passages.text: But when the men of that place asked about his wife, he said, “She is my sister.” For he was afraid to say, “She is my wife,” since he thought to himself, “The men of this place will kill me on account of Rebekah, because she is so beautiful.”
passages.sermon:
Isaac lived in Gerar.
The men of Gerar asked Isaac about his wife.
Isaac answered them.
He said, “She is my sister.”
Isaac did not say, “She is my wife.”
Isaac felt afraid.
He thought, “The men of this place might kill me because of Rebekah.”
Rebekah was very beautiful.
Isaac feared for his life because of her beauty.
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁאֲל֞וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ לְאִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא כִּ֤י יָרֵא֙ לֵאמֹ֣ר אִשְׁתִּ֔י פֶּן־ יַֽהַרְגֻ֜נִי אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמָּקוֹם֙ עַל־ רִבְקָ֔ה כִּֽי־ טוֹבַ֥ת מַרְאֶ֖ה הִֽיא׃

passages.text: When Isaac had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down from the window and was surprised to see Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah.
passages.sermon:
Isaac lived in Gerar for a long time.
Abimelech was the king of the Philistines.
Abimelech looked out through a window.
Abimelech saw Isaac with Rebekah.
Rebekah was Isaac’s wife.
Abimelech saw Isaac caressing Rebekah.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כִּ֣י אָֽרְכוּ־ ל֥וֹ שָׁם֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וַיַּשְׁקֵ֗ף אֲבִימֶ֙לֶךְ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים בְּעַ֖ד הַֽחַלּ֑וֹן וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה יִצְחָק֙ מְצַחֵ֔ק אֵ֖ת רִבְקָ֥ה אִשְׁתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Abimelech sent for Isaac and said, “So she is really your wife! How could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac replied, “Because I thought I might die on account of her.”
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the king of the Philistines.
Abimelech called Isaac.
Abimelech spoke to Isaac.
Abimelech said, “She is truly your wife.”
Abimelech asked, “Why did you say, ‘She is my sister’?”
Isaac answered Abimelech.
Isaac said, “I said it because I thought I might die because of her.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ לְיִצְחָ֗ק וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אַ֣ךְ הִנֵּ֤ה אִשְׁתְּךָ֙ הִ֔וא וְאֵ֥יךְ אָמַ֖רְתָּ אֲחֹ֣תִי הִ֑וא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ יִצְחָ֔ק כִּ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי פֶּן־ אָמ֖וּת עָלֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: “What is this you have done to us?” asked Abimelech. “One of the people could easily have slept with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.”
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the king of the Philistines.
Abimelech spoke to Isaac.
Abimelech said, “What have you done to us?”
Abimelech said, “One of the people almost slept with your wife.”
Abimelech said, “You would have brought guilt on us.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ מַה־ זֹּ֖את עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֑נוּ כִּ֠מְעַט שָׁכַ֞ב אַחַ֤ד הָעָם֙ אֶת־ אִשְׁתֶּ֔ךָ וְהֵבֵאתָ֥ עָלֵ֖ינוּ אָשָֽׁם׃

passages.text: So Abimelech warned all the people, saying, “Whoever harms this man or his wife will surely be put to death.”
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the king of the Philistines.
Abimelech spoke to all his people.
He gave them a command.
He said, “If anyone harms this man Isaac or his wife, that person will be put to death.”
passages.original: וַיְצַ֣ו אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר הַנֹּגֵ֜עַ בָּאִ֥ישׁ הַזֶּ֛ה וּבְאִשְׁתּ֖וֹ מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת׃

passages.text: Now Isaac sowed seed in the land, and that very year he reaped a hundredfold. And the LORD blessed him, and he became richer and richer, until he was exceedingly wealthy.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Abraham’s son.
Isaac sowed seed in that land.
That year, Isaac harvested one hundred times what he planted.
The LORD blessed Isaac.
Isaac became a great man.
Isaac continued to grow in wealth.
Isaac became extremely wealthy.
passages.original: וַיִּזְרַ֤ע יִצְחָק֙ בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֔וא וַיִּמְצָ֛א בַּשָּׁנָ֥ה הַהִ֖וא מֵאָ֣ה שְׁעָרִ֑ים וַֽיְבָרֲכֵ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה׃ וַיִּגְדַּ֖ל הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ הָלוֹךְ֙ וְגָדֵ֔ל עַ֥ד כִּֽי־ גָדַ֖ל מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: He owned so many flocks and herds and servants that the Philistines envied him.
passages.sermon:
Isaac lived in the land of the Philistines.
Isaac owned many flocks of sheep.
Isaac owned many herds of cattle.
Isaac had many servants.
The Philistines saw Isaac’s wealth.
The Philistines envied Isaac.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי־ ל֤וֹ מִקְנֵה־ צֹאן֙ וּמִקְנֵ֣ה בָקָ֔ר וַעֲבֻדָּ֖ה רַבָּ֑ה וַיְקַנְא֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

passages.text: So the Philistines took dirt and stopped up all the wells that his father’s servants had dug in the days of his father Abraham.
passages.sermon:
The Philistines acted against Isaac.
They filled all the wells with dirt.
Isaac’s father was Abraham.
Abraham’s servants had dug these wells during Abraham’s lifetime.
The Philistines stopped up every one of these wells.
passages.original: וְכָל־ הַבְּאֵרֹ֗ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י אָבִ֔יו בִּימֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יו סִתְּמ֣וּם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיְמַלְא֖וּם עָפָֽר׃

passages.text: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, “Depart from us, for you are much too powerful for us.”
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the king of the Philistines.
Isaac was a wealthy man.
Isaac owned many flocks, herds, and servants.
The Philistines envied Isaac.
Abimelech spoke to Isaac.
Abimelech said, “Leave us.”
Abimelech said, “You have become much stronger than we are.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ יִצְחָ֑ק לֵ֚ךְ מֵֽעִמָּ֔נוּ כִּֽי־ עָצַֽמְתָּ־ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: So Isaac left that place and encamped in the Valley of Gerar and settled there.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Abraham’s son.
Isaac left that place.
Isaac went to the Valley of Gerar.
Isaac set up his camp in the Valley of Gerar.
Isaac lived there.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֖ם יִצְחָ֑ק וַיִּ֥חַן בְּנַֽחַל־ גְּרָ֖ר וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Isaac reopened the wells that had been dug in the days of his father Abraham, which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham died. And he gave these wells the same names his father had given them.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Abraham’s son.
Abraham had dug wells during his lifetime.
The Philistines stopped up these wells after Abraham died.
Isaac returned to these wells.
Isaac reopened the wells.
Isaac gave the wells the same names that his father Abraham had given them.
passages.original: וַיָּ֨שָׁב יִצְחָ֜ק וַיַּחְפֹּ֣ר׀ אֶת־ בְּאֵרֹ֣ת הַמַּ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָֽפְרוּ֙ בִּימֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יו וַיְסַתְּמ֣וּם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים אַחֲרֵ֖י מ֣וֹת אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֤א לָהֶן֙ שֵׁמ֔וֹת כַּשֵּׁמֹ֕ת אֲשֶׁר־ קָרָ֥א לָהֶ֖ן אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Isaac’s servants dug in the valley and found a well of fresh water there.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Abraham’s son.
Isaac lived in the Valley of Gerar.
Isaac had servants.
Isaac’s servants dug in the valley.
They found a well there.
The well had fresh water.
passages.original: וַיַּחְפְּר֥וּ עַבְדֵֽי־ יִצְחָ֖ק בַּנָּ֑חַל וַיִּ֨מְצְאוּ־ שָׁ֔ם בְּאֵ֖ר מַ֥יִם חַיִּֽים׃

passages.text: But the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s herdsmen and said, “The water is ours!” So he named the well Esek, because they contended with him.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the son of Abraham.
Isaac had herdsmen.
Gerar was a place.
Gerar had herdsmen.
The herdsmen of Gerar argued with the herdsmen of Isaac.
The herdsmen of Gerar said, "The water is ours."
Isaac gave the well a name.
He called the well Esek.
He named it Esek because they contended with him.
passages.original: וַיָּרִ֜יבוּ רֹעֵ֣י גְרָ֗ר עִם־ רֹעֵ֥י יִצְחָ֛ק לֵאמֹ֖ר לָ֣נוּ הַמָּ֑יִם וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵֽׁם־ הַבְּאֵר֙ עֵ֔שֶׂק כִּ֥י הִֽתְעַשְּׂק֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then they dug another well and quarreled over that one also; so he named it Sitnah.
passages.sermon: Isaac’s servants dug another well.\r\nThe herdsmen of Gerar quarreled over this well also.\r\nIsaac named the well Sitnah.
passages.original: וַֽיַּחְפְּרוּ֙ בְּאֵ֣ר אַחֶ֔רֶת וַיָּרִ֖יבוּ גַּם־ עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמָ֖הּ שִׂטְנָֽה׃

passages.text: He moved on from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it. He named it Rehoboth and said, “At last the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.”
passages.sermon:
Isaac was a servant of God and the son of Abraham.
Isaac moved away from that place.
Isaac dug another well.
No one quarreled over this well.
Isaac named the well Rehoboth.
Isaac said, “Now the LORD has made room for us.
We will be fruitful in the land.”
passages.original: וַיַּעְתֵּ֣ק מִשָּׁ֗ם וַיַּחְפֹּר֙ בְּאֵ֣ר אַחֶ֔רֶת וְלֹ֥א רָב֖וּ עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ רְחֹב֔וֹת וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־ עַתָּ֞ה הִרְחִ֧יב יְהוָ֛ה לָ֖נוּ וּפָרִ֥ינוּ בָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: From there Isaac went up to Beersheba, and that night the LORD appeared to him and said, “I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your descendants for the sake of My servant Abraham.”
passages.sermon:
Isaac left that place.
He went to Beersheba.
That night, the LORD appeared to Isaac.
The LORD spoke to Isaac.
The LORD said, “I am the God of your father Abraham.
Do not be afraid.
I am with you.
I will bless you.
I will make your descendants many.
I will do this because of Abraham, my servant.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַל מִשָּׁ֖ם בְּאֵ֥ר שָֽׁבַע׃ וַיֵּרָ֨א אֵלָ֤יו יְהוָה֙ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָנֹכִ֕י אֱלֹהֵ֖י אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֑יךָ אַל־ תִּירָא֙ כִּֽי־ אִתְּךָ֣ אָנֹ֔כִי וּבֵֽרַכְתִּ֙יךָ֙ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֣י אֶֽת־ זַרְעֲךָ֔ בַּעֲב֖וּר אַבְרָהָ֥ם עַבְדִּֽי׃

passages.text: So Isaac built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD, and he pitched his tent there. His servants also dug a well there.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was Abraham’s son.
Isaac went to Beersheba.
Isaac built an altar there.
Isaac called on the name of the LORD.
Isaac set up his tent there.
Isaac’s servants dug a well there.
passages.original: וַיִּ֧בֶן שָׁ֣ם מִזְבֵּ֗חַ וַיִּקְרָא֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה וַיֶּט־ שָׁ֖ם אָהֳל֑וֹ וַיִּכְרוּ־ שָׁ֥ם עַבְדֵי־ יִצְחָ֖ק בְּאֵֽר׃

passages.text: Later, Abimelech came to Isaac from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army.
passages.sermon:
Abimelech was the king of Gerar.
Abimelech went to Isaac.
Abimelech came from Gerar.
Ahuzzath went with Abimelech.
Ahuzzath was Abimelech’s adviser.
Phicol also went with them.
Phicol was the commander of Abimelech’s army.
passages.original: וַאֲבִימֶ֕לֶךְ הָלַ֥ךְ אֵלָ֖יו מִגְּרָ֑ר וַאֲחֻזַּת֙ מֵֽרֵעֵ֔הוּ וּפִיכֹ֖ל שַׂר־ צְבָאֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “Why have you come to me?” Isaac asked them. “You hated me and sent me away.”
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the son of Abraham.
Isaac spoke to Abimelech, Ahuzzath, and Phicol.
Isaac asked them a question.
Isaac said, “Why have you come to me?”
Isaac reminded them of their actions.
Isaac said, “You hated me.”
Isaac said, “You sent me away from you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ יִצְחָ֔ק מַדּ֖וּעַ בָּאתֶ֣ם אֵלָ֑י וְאַתֶּם֙ שְׂנֵאתֶ֣ם אֹתִ֔י וַתְּשַׁלְּח֖וּנִי מֵאִתְּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: “We can plainly see that the LORD has been with you,” they replied. “We recommend that there should now be an oath between us and you. Let us make a covenant with you that you will not harm us, just as we have not harmed you but have done only good to you, sending you on your way in peace. And now you are blessed by the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Abimelech, Ahuzzath, and Phicol spoke to Isaac.
They said, “We see clearly that the LORD is with you.
We want to make an agreement with you.
Let there be an oath between us and you.
Let us make a covenant together.
Promise that you will not harm us.
We have not harmed you.
We have only done good to you.
We sent you away in peace.
Now the LORD has blessed you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ רָא֣וֹ רָאִינוּ֮ כִּֽי־ הָיָ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה׀ עִמָּךְ֒ וַנֹּ֗אמֶר תְּהִ֨י נָ֥א אָלָ֛ה בֵּינוֹתֵ֖ינוּ בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ וְנִכְרְתָ֥ה בְרִ֖ית עִמָּֽךְ׃ אִם־ תַּעֲשֵׂ֨ה עִמָּ֜נוּ רָעָ֗ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א נְגַֽעֲנ֔וּךָ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשִׂ֤ינוּ עִמְּךָ֙ רַק־ ט֔וֹב וַנְּשַׁלֵּֽחֲךָ֖ בְּשָׁל֑וֹם אַתָּ֥ה עַתָּ֖ה בְּר֥וּךְ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So Isaac prepared a feast for them, and they ate and drank.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was a patriarch and the son of Abraham.
Isaac prepared a feast for the men who came to him.
The men ate.
The men drank.
passages.original: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ לָהֶם֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וַיֹּאכְל֖וּ וַיִּשְׁתּֽוּ׃

passages.text: And they got up early the next morning and swore an oath to each other. Then Isaac sent them on their way, and they left him in peace.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the son of Abraham.
Isaac lived in the land of Canaan.
Isaac made a covenant with his neighbors.
They all woke up early in the morning.
Each man swore an oath to the other.
Isaac sent his neighbors away.
They left Isaac in peace.
passages.original: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּשָּׁבְע֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ לְאָחִ֑יו וַיְשַׁלְּחֵ֣ם יִצְחָ֔ק וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ מֵאִתּ֖וֹ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: On that same day, Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well they had dug. “We have found water!” they told him.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the son of Abraham.
Isaac had servants.
On that same day, Isaac’s servants came to him.
They had dug a well.
They told Isaac about the well.
They said to Isaac, “We have found water.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ עַבְדֵ֣י יִצְחָ֔ק וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ עַל־ אֹד֥וֹת הַבְּאֵ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָפָ֑רוּ וַיֹּ֥אמְרוּ ל֖וֹ מָצָ֥אנוּ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: So he called it Shibah, and to this day the name of the city is Beersheba.
passages.sermon:
Isaac was the son of Abraham.
Isaac’s servants found water in a well they dug.
Isaac named the well Shibah.
Because of this, the city is called Beersheba.
People still call it Beersheba today.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ שִׁבְעָ֑ה עַל־ כֵּ֤ן שֵׁם־ הָעִיר֙ בְּאֵ֣ר שֶׁ֔בַע עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

passages.text: When Esau was forty years old, he took as his wives Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite.
passages.sermon:
Esau was the son of Isaac and Rebekah.
Esau reached the age of forty years.
Esau chose wives for himself.
He married Judith.
Judith was the daughter of Beeri.
Beeri was a Hittite.
Esau also married Basemath.
Basemath was the daughter of Elon.
Elon was a Hittite.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י עֵשָׂו֙ בֶּן־ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וַיִּקַּ֤ח אִשָּׁה֙ אֶת־ יְהוּדִ֔ית בַּת־ בְּאֵרִ֖י הַֽחִתִּ֑י וְאֶת־ בָּ֣שְׂמַ֔ת בַּת־ אֵילֹ֖ן הַֽחִתִּֽי׃

passages.text: And they brought grief to Isaac and Rebekah.
passages.sermon:
Esau married Judith and Basemath.
Judith was the daughter of Beeri the Hittite.
Basemath was the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
These wives caused grief to Isaac.
These wives caused grief to Rebekah.
passages.original: וַתִּהְיֶ֖יןָ מֹ֣רַת ר֑וּחַ לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּלְרִבְקָֽה׃ס
